title: Mapo Tofu Vegetarian

Expert Tips for the Best Vegetarian Mapo Tofu
seo.imageAlt: A bowl of vibrant vegetarian mapo tofu with silken tofu, chili oil, and Sichuan peppercorns, garnished with green onions.
seo.imageCaption: Our delicious Vegetarian Mapo Tofu is packed with spicy, savory, and numbing flavors – a true Chinese classic!

description: A beloved Sichuan classic reimagined for vegetarians, this Mapo Tofu delivers a delightful kick with its signature numbing spice and rich, savory flavors. Tender silken tofu cubes are simmered in a fiery, aromatic sauce, creating an unforgettable and deeply satisfying meatless meal.

instructions.title: Prepare Tofu and Aromatics
instructions.text: Gently drain the tofu and cut it into 3/4-inch cubes. If using silken tofu, you may blanch it in hot salted water for 2-3 minutes to firm it slightly, then drain. Mince the garlic and ginger. Rinse the fermented black beans and lightly mash them. Prepare your cornstarch slurry by mixing cornstarch with water in a small bowl.

instructions.title: Toast Sichuan Peppercorns
instructions.text: Heat a dry wok or skillet over medium heat. Add the whole Sichuan peppercorns and toast for 2-3 minutes until fragrant and slightly smoking. Remove from heat, let cool slightly, then grind into a fine powder using a mortar and pestle or a spice grinder. Set aside.

instructions.title: Sauté Aromatics and Pastes
instructions.text: Heat vegetable oil in the same wok over medium-high heat. Add minced garlic and ginger and stir-fry for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add the Pixian doubanjiang and fermented black beans. Stir-fry for 1-2 minutes until the oil turns red and fragrant. If using vegetarian ground 'meat', add it now and cook until lightly browned, about 3-4 minutes.

instructions.title: Build the Sauce Base
instructions.text: Pour in the vegetable broth, light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, and sugar. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer, scraping any bits from the bottom of the wok. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed, keeping in mind the chili bean paste is quite salty.

instructions.title: Add Tofu and Simmer
instructions.text: Carefully add the tofu cubes to the simmering sauce. Gently stir to coat the tofu, but avoid overmixing to prevent breaking the cubes. Allow the tofu to simmer in the sauce for 5-7 minutes, letting it absorb the flavors.

instructions.title: Thicken the Sauce
instructions.text: Give the cornstarch slurry a quick stir, then slowly pour it into the simmering tofu, stirring gently but constantly until the sauce thickens to your desired consistency. You may not need all of the slurry. The sauce should be glossy and cling to the tofu.

instructions.title: Finish and Serve
instructions.text: Stir in the ground Sichuan peppercorn powder and sesame oil. Remove from heat immediately. Transfer the Mapo Tofu to a serving dish. Garnish generously with chopped scallions and a drizzle of chili oil, if desired. Serve hot with steamed white rice.

tips: To achieve the authentic 'ma la' (numbing and spicy) flavor, do not skip the Sichuan peppercorns. Toasting them properly before grinding is key to releasing their full aroma.
For the best flavor, use authentic Pixian Doubanjiang (Sichuan chili bean paste). It provides a depth of umami and spice that cannot be easily replicated by other chili pastes.
Handle the tofu gently after adding it to the sauce. Silken tofu is delicate, and a gentle push-and-fold motion with your spatula is better than vigorous stirring to keep the cubes intact.
